claim: For integers \(N\ge 3\) and \(2\le m\le N-1\), let \(F_N=(\omega^{rs})_{r,s\in\mathbb Z_N}\) with \(\omega=e^{-2\pi i/N}\), and select the three rows \(\mathcal M=\{0,1,m\}\). The resulting \(3\times N\) harmonic frame is full spark if and only if \(\gcd(N,m)\le 2\) and \(\gcd(N,m-1)\le 2\); equivalently, it is full spark if and only if \(\mathcal M\) is uniformly distributed over every divisor of \(N\).
integrity: The infinite result is proved by an exact determinant/geometric-sum argument. The accompanying checker uses exact integer polynomial and residue arithmetic, with no floating-point acceptance decisions.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats the two-parameter three-row family \(\{0,1,m\}\), not arbitrary row sets. Finite verifier sweeps are regression checks only. Literature search cannot exclude differently phrased or poorly indexed prior statements.
title: A complete full-spark criterion for every three-row Fourier pattern \(\{0,1,m\}\)
